restaurants.notes: SOURCE METHOD: fetched raw HTML of every page on danvilleharvest.com with curl -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" (site nav has only 5 pages: /, /menu, /events, /contact, /reservations; /about, /gallery, /press, /our-story, /private-events all return 404). Extracted , data-src, srcset, og:image, Squarespace assetUrl JSON and CSS background-image; resolved and de-duplicated to canonical Squarespace CDN bases; requested each at ?format=2500w. Every URL below was HEAD-checked with curl -sIL (all 200) and then downloaded and measured with Pillow, and every image was visually inspected before being described. No Instagram/Facebook CDN URLs are included. FORMAT NEGOTIATION: images.squarespace-cdn.com content-negotiates. With Accept: image/webp it returns image/webp (e.g. Harvest_6_15_23-94 = 711,138 B WEBP); with a plain jpeg Accept it returns image/jpeg (772,706 B). The content_type/bytes recorded here are the JPEG/PNG variant. Pixel dimensions are identical either way. The originals were uploaded at 2000 px on the long edge, so ?format=2500w returns the full 2000x1333 (or 1333x2000) original - there is nothing larger. OWN PHOTOGRAPHY: all 24 restaurant photos on the site come from one professional shoot, filenames Harvest_6_15_23-N.jpg (shot 15 June 2023). Full set of N used on the site: 1, 9, 40, 47, 56, 64, 70, 73, 85, 86, 91, 94, 106, 127, 128, 130, 131, 134, 139, 152, 156, 158, 159, 160. All are included below. The site has no gallery/lightbox page holding additional images. OG:IMAGE PER PAGE (all verified 200, served from static1.squarespace.com at ?format=1500w; note the site declares them with an http:// scheme, https works fine): / -> Harvest_6_15_23-160.jpg (recorded above as og_image); /menu -> .../6494f6b74cda395e3373f030/1687484087914/Harvest_6_15_23-64.jpg; /events -> .../6494f6ca6d6d73138103e1d3/1687484106288/Harvest_6_15_23-128.jpg; /contact -> .../6494f6f7f3a6a6170b0b3cab/1687484151307/Harvest_6_15_23-1.jpg; /reservations -> .../6494f69dcfb66a798e27a618/1687484061743/Harvest_6_15_23-156.jpg. LOGOS: two official variants, both RGBA transparent PNG and both LIGHT-coloured, so neither will read on a white directory card - header wordmark Danville_Harvest_conceptlogo.png is pure white (579x115), footer mark Harvest_yellow.png is cream (350x201, barn + tree illustration above the wordmark). A BLACK-on-white version of the same barn logo (992x618 PNG) is hosted third-party at danvillesocial.com and is included below as the usable light-background variant. NAME HISTORY (important for dated photos): the restaurant opened in 2016 as "Almanac" and was renamed "Harvest"/"Danville Harvest" over a trademark issue - same owners, same 500 Hartz Ave building (confirmed on the architect's project page, laraarchitecture.squarespace.com/harvest-restaurant: "Harvest (formerly called Almanac) was a complete renovation of a 3000-square-foot restaurant... The historic building situated on a prominent corner of Danville's downtown district"). Any third-party photo showing an "almanac" sign or white-subway-tile / Tolix-chair interior is this restaurant pre-refresh, not a different business. EXTERIOR / HARTZ + CHURCH CORNER: confirmed the building sits on the Hartz Ave & Church St corner. The four best corner shots are the restaurant's own: Harvest_6_15_23-94 (golden hour, tight on the corner sign), -156 (blue hour, whole corner lit), -106 (wide, from across the intersection) and -152 (side patio at night). The one press exterior found is Food Gal's HarvestExterior.jpg (night, corner, diners on the patio, USPS mailbox) but it is only 760x427. PRESS SEARCHED: danvillesanramon.com (no Harvest-specific article; the 4 May 2026 Rancho Cantina piece only name-checks "Danville Harvest at 500 Hartz Ave." and its photos are of 501 Hartz across the street). Diablo Magazine's site returned HTTP 429 to every request and could not be read. Hoodline, Patch and Bay Area Telegraph searches returned nothing on this restaurant. Yelp and Tripadvisor were not used (403/blocked, and user photos are last resort). The architect's page cites two 2016 print pieces I could not retrieve: East Bay Times, 22 Sep 2016, "Plenty to Love at Danville's Almanac Bistro" and Diablo Magazine, Oct 2016, "A Sweet Success: Farmers Almanac offers Bay Area cuisine with a shot of Southern comfort". VERIFIED BUT NOT LISTED BELOW (all HEAD-200 and measured, omitted to keep the list usable): - Food Gal (2018 review, https://www.foodgal.com/2018/05/a-taste-of-the-seasons-at-danville-harvest/) dish photos, author's own captions: Cauliflower.jpg 760x517 304,866B "a simple yet striking roasted cauliflower"; Wagyu.jpg 760x474 439,677B sliced wagyu sirloin with arugula and corn succotash; Lamb.jpg 740x1079 667,459B lamb with carrot puree; BeetSoup.jpg 760x658 424,955B; PorkTenderloin.jpg 680x946 604,450B; ShrimpKamut.jpg 760x522 386,612B; BasilPotdeCreme.jpg 660x955 690,012B; ChessPie.jpg 760x496 400,090B. All under https://www.foodgal.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/. These are 2018 dishes; most are no longer on the June 2026 menus, so use with care. - Lara Architecture project page, https://laraarchitecture.squarespace.com/harvest-restaurant (all under https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/65b48a4b1e423855b3c1546a/): 776d0644-5a9d-45f9-9d5f-b8d70481b30f/row-of-dining-tables-with-a-view-of-the-open-kitchen-in-the-background.jpg 1400x2100 213,321B; 0f2a761d-aedb-4bbe-8aec-536e9f8d486b/built-in-tuffted-leather-bench-seat-table-in-corner-next-to-a-wall-of-windows-at-harvest-restaurant-in-danville.jpg 1400x2418 344,542B; 36962d95-748b-47d1-9c08-8561ce4ecf48/diners-sitting-at-countertop-that-faces-into-the-restaurant-kitchen-as-they-talk-with-a-smiling-chef.jpg 1800x1295 334,048B; 37a47966-9c32-47bc-877a-0d579a0440ac/interior-entry-area-at-harvest-restaurant.jpg 1400x2024 257,680B; c6fa79ab-e599-41f3-a017-7f8bdf242664/entry-with-wood-table-and-chandelier-at-harvest-restaurant.jpg 1400x2075 324,715B; 64ee91f0-7a0f-4517-b3b4-2aae7aae60f9/two-chefs-work-side-by-side-in-open-kitchen-with-view-of-diners-inside-the-dining-room-at-harvest-restaurant-in-Danville.jpg 1800x1200 312,941B. - danvillesocial.com directory listing (https://www.danvillesocial.com/directory/danville-harvest/) also hosts five 2019-era amateur customer snapshots under https://www.danvillesocial.com/php_partials/uploads/2019/01/: Danville-Harvest-1.jpg 1000x1000 (deviled eggs on a periwinkle plate, an "almanac" menu visible), -2.jpg 750x1000 (charcuterie board, dim), -3.jpg 750x1000 (eggs benedict), -4.jpg 1000x562 (cobb salad), -5.jpg 750x1000 (entry doors under an "almanac" sign). Low quality / obsolete branding - last resort only. CAVEATS: rights were not cleared for any third-party image; Food Gal and Lara Architecture photos are the photographers'/publishers' and would need permission. The Lara Architecture set documents the 2016 build-out (Almanac signage, white subway tile, Tolix chairs) - the dining rooms have since been re-clad in chevron reclaimed wood with leather nailhead chairs and linen drapes, so those photos no longer match the current room. The chef pictured in Food Gal's TimHumphrey.jpg is Tim Humphrey, exec chef in 2018; the current exec chef is Noe Briseno, so do not caption it as the current chef. No current-day chef or staff portrait exists on the restaurant's own site.

images.description: Golden-hour exterior of the corner building, shot from the sidewalk. The glassed-in porch dining room with weathered timber posts fills the frame, the large painted white-on-grey 'harvest' sign hangs on the corner, cafe string lights run overhead, shingle roof and navy patio umbrellas above, a bed of blooming lavender and ornamental grasses along the low stucco wall, a sycamore trunk at left. Site alt text: 'Danville Harvest Exterior'. Best daytime exterior available.

Blue-hour / twilight exterior of the whole corner: deep blue sky, the yellow clapboard building glowing warm from inside, string lights strung across the patio, the 'harvest' sign lit on the corner fence, navy umbrellas, uplit planting bed, blue USPS mailbox and a wine barrel at left, brick-banded crosswalk in the foreground. og:image of the /reservations page. Strongest evening hero.

Wide establishing shot taken from across the intersection at dusk, showing the full corner of Hartz Ave and Church St: the yellow single-storey building with dark shingle roof under mature street trees, the 'harvest' sign on the porch fence, navy and cream umbrellas, a US flag on the neighbouring facade, blue USPS mailbox, two green trash bins, the brick crosswalk and street in the foreground. Site alt text: 'The view of Danville Harvest as seen from across the street.'

The side patio at night: rows of empty slatted-wood tables and chairs on a paved terrace, a retractable white awning and cafe string lights overhead, wall-mounted overhead heaters, the yellow clapboard wall with a run of French doors glowing warm, guests visible seated inside, picket fence and ornamental grasses along the sidewalk edge. Site alt text: 'The side patio area as seen at night.'

Daytime patio-dining scene on a weathered wood outdoor table: a glazed bone-in pork chop over sweet-potato puree with greens and chutney on a rustic cream plate, a coupe cocktail full of cloudy orange liquid at right, a tall lemon-and-mint highball at left, a plate of fried croquettes with citrus salad at lower right, a bud vase of pink and magenta blooms, parked cars and green street trees blurred behind. Site alt text: 'Drinks and entrees on our outside patio'. Good for conveying the sidewalk-patio experience.

Back dining area looking down a long row of two-top tables: tan leather nailhead-trim chairs, wood table tops set with dark folded napkins and single pink peonies in glass bud vases, black industrial dome pendants, floor-to-ceiling linen drapes gathered and tied with rope, blue tufted banquettes on the right, and a white-framed pass-through window with stacked crockery on the left. Site alt text: 'Back Dining Area'. Best interior hero.

Wide, evenly lit view of the main back dining room: a chevron/herringbone reclaimed-wood feature wall hung with two round mirrors and small framed photographs, a long grey tufted banquette beneath it, tan leather nailhead chairs at wood tables with pink peonies, tall multi-pane windows with linen drapes at left looking onto the street, black dome pendants, polished concrete floor. Site alt text: 'Our main dining area in the back of our restaurant. Great for private events.'

The full bar, shot square-on: tiered timber back-bar shelving packed with whiskey and spirit bottles and lit from beneath, suspended blackened-steel racks holding more bottles and hanging stemware, a bank of draft taps and a small oak barrel on the counter, a wall-mounted TV, sage-green upholstered swivel bar stools along a thick dark wood bar top, glass-front under-bar coolers and a wine fridge. Supports the 'largest whiskey selection in the Tri-Valley' claim.

Front bar-lounge room looking out from behind the bar top: sage-green bar chairs along a thick wood counter in the foreground, a caramel leather button-tufted banquette running along the far wall with wood two-tops in front of it, chevron reclaimed-wood wall panels, a suspended glassware rack, a small chandelier, a TV, a trailing pothos plant, framed pictures, and windows onto the street. Site alt text: 'The view of our front dining area with full bar and tables.'

Vertical dining-room shot down a row of wood tables set with dark napkins and pink peonies in bud vases, tan leather nailhead chairs, black dome pendants, gathered linen drapes at right, and a large weathered metal 'COOK' sign on the back wall above an opening to the front room and a street-facing window. Portrait orientation - good for a mobile or sidebar slot, too dark and tall for a wide hero. og:image of the /events page.

Moody vertical view into the curtained private-dining nook: heavy linen drapes tied back on both sides framing a row of set tables with tan leather chairs and pink peonies, the chevron wood wall and grey banquette at the far end, warm pendant light pooling on the tables, the pass-through window and shelving glowing at right. Deliberately dark and atmospheric. Site alt text: 'Our back dining area. Perfect for private parties. Links to Events page.'

The restaurant's own homepage hero and site-wide og:image: two deeply seared scallops on a bed of creamy risotto with diced vegetables, crowned with a tall tangle of red-stemmed micro greens, in a dark blue-black ceramic bowl on a walnut table; a glass of white wine, a second plated dish and a lime wedge blurred behind. Shallow depth of field, warm side light.

A thick block of glazed braised short rib set on a nest of wide fettuccine and wilted spinach in a dark speckled bowl, topped with a crisp tangle of fried onion strings and lemon zest, on an outdoor wood table; a pink grapefruit cocktail, a green cocktail, magenta and pink blooms in bud vases and a parked car all blurred behind. Site alt text: 'Glazed Short Ribs'. Matches the menu's Braised Short Ribs and Short Rib Bites.

Overhead three-quarter shot of two dishes and a drink on a wood table: a seasonal salad in a dark speckled bowl (butter lettuce, mango, blueberries, strawberries, cucumber, shaved onion, flax seed) beside a terracotta plate of golden fried chicken with lemon wheels, rosemary, green beans and cream sauce, with a rocks glass of an old-fashioned garnished with a citrus twist between them. Site alt text: 'Our fresh seasonal salad and fried chicken.'

Action shot: a hand holding a kitchen blowtorch, blue flame lit, searing a rosemary sprig planted in a mound of craggy golden fried chicken with lemon wheels and green beans in a pale cream sauce on a terracotta-orange plate; a bright red cocktail in a cut-glass tumbler at left, a bowl of chopped salad at right, dark slate-blue background. Site alt text: 'Fried Chicken Dinner. Links to Dinner menu in a new browser tab.' Most dramatic of the food images.

A tall, glossy glazed bone-in pork chop resting on wilted spinach and a swipe of sweet-potato/squash puree, topped with a chunky apple-onion chutney and micro herbs, with a pool of dark jus alongside, on a rustic speckled cream plate; a stemmed glass of beer or wine and folded napkin blurred behind, warm window light across a wood table. og:image of the /menu page.

A crisp tempura-battered stuffed squash blossom propped on a nest of frisee and micro greens with blistered cherry tomatoes and green beans, over a broad pool of orange romesco-style sauce dusted with paprika, on a rectangular white ceramic plate. Clean, high-contrast subject on a simple plate - the easiest of the food shots to crop or cut out. Site alt text: 'Squash Blossom Brunch Dish. Links to Brunch menu in a new browser tab.'

A cheese and charcuterie board laid out on a long wooden paddle: blue cheese, wedges of hard and semi-hard cheese, sliced green apple, dried apricots, spiced nuts, a green olive, pickled red onion, toasted crostini and a small copper ramekin of honey; a pink cocktail with a lime wheel at upper left, an empty teal plate, and a white plate of golden fried croquettes with grapefruit-and-fennel citrus salad at right, all on a weathered grey outdoor table. Good 'shareable plates / happy hour' image.

A hand pours amber whiskey from a glass carafe into a fluted crystal rocks glass holding a large clear ice cube and a citrus twist, wisps of smoke curling off the surface, on a dark polished wood bar; magenta chrysanthemums in a mason jar and a folded napkin with cutlery behind, the pourer's red-and-white floral sleeve at right. Site alt text: 'Manhattan Cocktail'. Best bar-programme image.

A vivid ruby-red cocktail in a cut-crystal rocks glass garnished with a rosemary sprig, sharply lit against a dark slate-blue background; a coupe of dark cherry-garnished Manhattan-style cocktail at left, a cloudy amber sour out of focus at right, a plate of grilled asparagus salad and croquettes with citrus salad in the lower frame. Strong colour, dark simple backdrop - crops well.

Two golden seared scallops on herbed risotto with halved cherry tomatoes and a spray of red-stemmed micro greens in a dark ceramic bowl on a wood table, another plate and a wine glass blurred behind. Same dish and setup as Harvest_6_15_23-160 but lit darker and moodier; use -160 instead unless a low-key version is wanted. Site alt text: 'Scallop Lunch dish. Links to Lunch Menu in a new browser tab.'

Very shallow-focus table scene: a grilled asparagus salad with draped prosciutto, shaved hard cheese, pine nuts and mixed leaves on a white rectangular plate in the foreground (partly cropped by the frame edge), with an Aperol-style orange spritz, a dark cocktail, a plate of croquettes with citrus salad and a napkin-and-fork setting all softly blurred behind. Atmospheric rather than a clean dish shot. Site alt text: 'A fresh asparagus and prosciutto dish.'

Overhead, dramatically side-lit dessert: a custard (creme brulee style) in a white ramekin dusted heavily with powdered sugar and topped with a single strawberry slice, sitting on a walnut serving board scattered with more powdered sugar alongside two shards of biscotti/shortbread; a dark Manhattan-style cocktail in a coupe with a citrus twist at upper left, a knife and napkin at lower left, a water glass upper right, dark wood table. Site alt text: 'Our creme brulee dessert dish'. Note: no dessert menu is published on the site.

Table-setting detail on a reclaimed wood table: two place settings of stacked speckled plates with folded charcoal napkins and silverware, a single lilac chrysanthemum in a dimpled amber bud vase and a jar of magenta and cream chrysanthemums, backlit by the white-framed multi-pane porch windows and the yellow clapboard wall behind. Calm, low-clutter brand image with a simple background - good for a card or section break. og:image of the /contact page.

Official site header logo: horizontal wordmark, small spaced capitals 'DANVILLE' above a large rough typewriter-style lowercase 'harvest'. Pure WHITE artwork on a transparent background (PNG, RGBA) - invisible on white, needs a dark or photographic backdrop. Appears in the header of all five site pages.

Official site footer logo: a hand-drawn barn with an open door and a small tree on a ground line, with 'DANVILLE' set into the ground line at left and the large typewriter-style 'harvest' wordmark beneath. Cream / off-white artwork on a transparent background (PNG, RGBA) - also needs a dark backdrop. Appears in the footer of all five site pages.

WARNING - STOCK PHOTO, NOT DANVILLE HARVEST. Licensed Unsplash image (filename unsplash-image-xIFbDeGcy44.jpg) used as a decorative section background on the menu page: two shallow stone-coloured bowls of a vegetable/crudo dish on a rough wooden table with a glass of white wine, a glass of red, a jar of blue wildflowers and an antique fork. Recorded only so it is not mistaken for the restaurant's own photography - do not use it on the directory listing.

Press photo (Food Gal review, May 2018) of the Hartz Ave / Church St corner at night: the yellow clapboard building lit up, cafe string lights strung over the front patio, the black-and-white 'harvest' sign on the picket fence, guests dining at tables under furled and open umbrellas, the blue USPS mailbox and sycamore trunk at left, a second 'harvest' sign over the side entrance. Article caption: 'Located on a corner with plenty of outside seating for those balmy Danville evenings.' Only 760x427, so not usable as a hero - the restaurant's own -156 and -106 cover the same view at 2000 px. Rights not cleared.

Press photo (Food Gal, May 2018) of the dining room: a black-and-white damask curtain tied back with twine on a timber post, dark button-tufted leather banquette, wood tables, metal Tolix-style chairs, a rolling library ladder, wood-plank ceiling with track lighting, and a fiddle-leaf fig by the service station. HISTORICAL - the room has since been redecorated (plain linen drapes, tan leather nailhead chairs, chevron wood wall); do not present as current. Article caption: 'The dining room.'

Press photo (Food Gal, May 2018) of six golden-fried hushpuppy spheres on a periwinkle-blue rectangular plate with a chive-topped quenelle of butter/aioli behind, on a wood table. Article caption: 'Hushpuppies that never leave the menu' - the hushpuppies are still on the current dinner, lunch and brunch menus, so this is the only photograph found anywhere of the restaurant's signature dish. The restaurant's own site has no hushpuppy shot. Rights not cleared.

Press portrait (Food Gal, May 2018) of a smiling bearded chef in a white chef coat embroidered 'harvest' on the chest and his name on the pocket, standing at the kitchen pass with the steel equipment racks behind him. Article caption: 'Chef Tim Humphrey.' DO NOT USE AS A CURRENT CHEF PORTRAIT - the executive chef today is Noe Briseno. Recorded only as the sole staff photograph found; the restaurant's own site publishes none.

BLACK-on-white version of the restaurant's barn logo - the same artwork as the official cream Harvest_yellow.png (line-drawn barn with open door, small tree, 'DANVILLE' in the ground line, big typewriter 'harvest' beneath) rendered in solid black on a white field at 992x618. Hosted by the danvillesocial.com local directory, alt text 'Harvest restaurant in Danville CA'. This is the only dark-on-light logo variant found and is the practical choice for a white directory card, but it is a third-party copy - ask the restaurant for the original asset before publishing.

Professional architectural photo from the project page of Lara Architecture, who designed the restaurant: a server in apron and dress carrying plates down the timber steps of the front porch onto the sunlit patio, where guests sit at wood tables under big cream umbrellas behind a low picket fence with lavender planted along it, mature sycamores overhead, the yellow clapboard facade behind. No signage visible so it does not date itself, but it documents the 2016 build-out (then trading as Almanac). Best third-party daytime patio image. Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

Architect's photo of the front entrance: a dark steel awning with cut-metal letters spelling 'almanac' over open dark-framed French doors set into the pale yellow clapboard facade, lantern sconces either side, dappled sycamore shade and blue sky above. HISTORICAL - shows the building under its original name before the rename to Harvest, so it cannot be used as a current exterior. Useful only as evidence of the building/facade design. Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

Architect's photo of the bar shot square-on in daylight: white subway-tiled back wall, suspended blackened-steel racks holding spirits and rows of stemware, a bank of draft taps on a stainless plinth, back-bar bottle shelves, a white jug of sunflowers and a bowl of lemons on the thick wood counter, sage-green bar chairs across the foreground. Same bar as the restaurant's own -134 but brighter and pre-refresh (2016 build). Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

Architect's photo of the open kitchen from the dining room: cooks working behind a long white counter under custom blackened-steel equipment racks stacked with pans, baskets, crockery and bread, big black dome pendants and heat lamps overhead, white subway tile throughout, and a row of wood two-top tables with metal Tolix chairs and small potted succulents in the foreground. The clearest existing view of the on-display kitchen. HISTORICAL (2016 build-out, pre-rename). Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

Architect's wide interior of the main dining room: dark green button-tufted leather banquettes against a grey wall hung with two round mirrors and framed pictures (the same mirrors still hang on today's chevron wood wall), heavy reclaimed timber posts and beams under a wood-plank ceiling, black articulated wall lamps and dome pendants, and along the right a white subway-tiled kitchen counter with a reclaimed-wood shelf, faced by wood tables and Tolix chairs on polished concrete. HISTORICAL (2016 build-out, pre-rename) - the walls and seating have since changed. Rights are the architect's/photographer's.
